about.label: About the auction
about.title: Things with a story
about.p1: , Rector of the Kyiv School of Economics, is giving his personal belongings to a charity auction. Each one becomes a separate lot, and all proceeds go to a common cause.
about.p2: We want taking part to be simple and the result to be transparent: photos, descriptions and starting prices are published only after the Rector's Office approves them, and a report on the funds will appear here after the final.

start.a: The public start is planned for early November. The Rector's Office will confirm the exact date.

photos.a: A bid is a commitment to buy the lot if it wins. Payment is due within 7 days of closing.

bidding.a: Sign in by email or with Google, open a lot and place a bid: it must beat the current one by at least the lot's step. A bid in the last minutes extends bidding so everyone can respond.

who.a: The auction is open to everyone: students, alumni, partners and friends of KSE. Registration terms will be announced before the start.

offline.a: The main format is closing the bidding online. A get-together on the KSE campus is still to be confirmed.

delivery.q: How do I get a lot I won?

funds.a: The cause and the account are still being confirmed. They will be published once confirmed, together with the report.

sections.p: Anyone aged 18 or over who has registered on the site and agreed to these rules.
Each bid must beat the current one by at least the lot's step. The starting price and step are shown on each lot page. A bid placed in the last 5 minutes extends that lot's closing time by 5 minutes.
By bidding you commit to buy the lot if your bid wins. Refusing to pay leads to your account being blocked.
Bidding closes automatically at the stated time, by the server clock. The highest valid bid at closing wins.
The winner pays within 7 days of closing by bank transfer to the fundraising account. The Rector's Office will send the details.
Pick-up from the KSE Rector's Office in Kyiv, or Nova Poshta delivery at the buyer's expense. International delivery by arrangement.
The lot may be offered to the bidder with the next highest bid.
The auction may be changed or cancelled for objective reasons, including the war or the security situation.
Your name, email and phone, and your bids. A nickname, anonymity setting and consent to publish a photo are optional.
So you can bid and get notifications about your bids, and so the Rector's Office can contact winners about payment and handover.
Only the auction's administrators at the KSE Rector's Office see your contacts. The public bid history shows only your nickname, your first name with a surname initial, or "anonymous", as you choose.
Data is stored on secure servers in the EU and is never shared with third parties.
You can ask us to delete your data by writing to the Rector's Office. After the auction ends, data is deleted within an agreed period.
